issues.legal_issue: Statutory vesting of enemy property in the Custodian does not transfer ownership to the Custodian or the Union, but places the property in the Custodian’s trusteeship for management and administration.
Enemy property vested in the Custodian is not property of the Union and therefore is not exempt from State or local taxes under Article 285(1) of the Constitution.
Article 285(2) permits taxation of Union property only where its requirements are met, and does not apply to enemy property that is not Union property.
A private lessee or occupier of enemy property is liable for property and other local taxes imposed in accordance with law.

The Municipal Corporation may collect property tax, water tax, sewerage charges, and other local taxes on the property prospectively from fiscal year 2024–2025, while amounts already paid are not refundable and no earlier unissued demands may be raised.
